sources_considered.why: Original survey publisher reports adoption and workflow integration.
Separate original survey distinguishes daily use from intended adoption.
Independent randomized study limits any inference of universal productivity gains.

evidence_items.locator: Massive adoption meets major productivity gains
evidence_items.explanation: The survey of nearly 5,000 technology professionals reports extensive adoption and a median two hours of daily AI use in core workflows. This supports substantial changes in development practice, although the sample includes roles beyond developers.

evidence_items.locator: 3.1 Sentiment and usage — AI tools in the development process
evidence_items.explanation: Daily use by a majority of professional respondents supports substantial workflow penetration. This figure measures actual use, unlike the survey's separate combined figure for use or planned use.

This randomized study found a slowdown for experienced developers working in familiar repositories. It challenges a universal productivity interpretation, but does not contradict widespread adoption or changed workflows.

unresolved_gaps: The surveys are not a census of the industry and rely on self-report.
Annual evidence does not measure the precise industry state on April 27, 2026.
No agreed measure defines an industry revolution.
